texts.preamble: Arif Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 December, 2018 1 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh M.Cr.C. No.46412/2018 (Himanshu Bansal Vs. State of M.P.) & M.Cr.C. No.48140/2018 (Arif Khan Vs. State of M.P.) Gwalior, dated: 13.12.2018 Shri Gaurav Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioner in M.Cr.C. No.46412/2018. Shri Suresh Agrawal, learned counsel for the petitioner in M.Cr.C. No.48140/2018. Ms. Ami Prabal, learned Deputy Advocate General for the respondent/State. Both the aforesaid cases relate to the same crime number against both the petitioners who are partners in business and therefore have been heard analogously and are being decided by the present common order. These are 1st applications u/S.438 Cr.P.C. filed by the petitioners for grant of anticipatory bail. Petitioners apprehend arrest in connection with offences punishable u/Ss.270, 272, 273, 420 of Ipc r/w 57, 59, 63 and 64 of Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006 registered as Crime No.1132/2018 at Police Station City Kotwali Morena. Learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the applications and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out. The allegation against both the petitioners is that they were found manufacturing the spurious paneer with the help of synthetic material such as caustic soda and certain chemicals with milk as not one of the ingredients. The prosecution has alleged offence of cheating punishable u/S.420 o Ipc along with the aforesaid offence probably with intent to render the offences non-bailable. Pertinently, all other offences except Sec.420 of Ipc alleged against petitioners are bailable as punishment provided for the same are not more than 3 months. Arif Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 December, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121311102/ 1 Learned counsel for petitioners by relying upon a Single Bench decision of the High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench rendered in W.P. No.102964/2018 on 28.06.2018 contends that in allegation of the nature alleged against petitioners under Food and Safety Act, offence of cheating is not attracted. This Court was initially of the prima facie view that the offence of cheating does not appear to be attracted as the definition of cheating u/S.415 of Ipc essentially requires as a per-requisites that there should be a person indulging in cheating and another who is cheated. In the incident, allegation discloses that mere manufacturing of spurious paneer is alleged with no allegation of any other person having been deceived to part with his property by purchase of spurious paneer. After hearing learned counsel for the State, Smt. Ami Prabal, Deputy Advocate General who has opposed the grant of anticipatory bail by raising the plea of larger public interest, this Court deems it appropriate to indulge in a deeper probe to ascertain the involvement of the element of cheating or not. To ascertain as to whether the offence of cheating punishable u/S. 420 Ipc is made out or not, it would be appropriate to closely scan the definition of cheating in Sec. 415 Ipc which is reproduced below:- Sec. 415. Cheating.--Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to "cheat". Explanation.--A dishonest concealment of facts is a deception within the meaning of this section. Cheating is constituted when deceit is exercised by any person in a fraudulent or dishonest manner resulting in inducing another who is deceived to deliver any property to any person or to consent that any person shall retain any property or intentionally induces a person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he was not so deceived. The definition culminates with the stipulation that such act or omission on the part of the person deceived either causes or is likely to cause harm in mind, reputation or property to the person deceived. Explanation to Sec. 415 Ipc further clarifies that dishonest concealment of facts is a deception within the meaning of cheating. In the instant case, the Fir dated 20/10/2018 is lodge based on the complaint of the complainant who is a Food Safety Officer of District Morena which is founded on the revelation made on raid carried out by Tehsildar on the request of the Food Safety Officer at the firm-Sai Baba Milk Dairy Product situated in an industrial area of District Morena.
